text: On the night of December 16, members of the Sons of Liberty boarded the ship Dartmouth in Boston. They threw 340 or 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor.
In November 1773 the merchant ship Dartmouth arrived in Boston harbor. It carried the first shipment of tea made under the terms of the Tea Act.
In 1750, Paul Revere was 15 years old. He was part of the first group to ring the new bells at Christ Church in Boston, the Old North Church.
Paul Revere's midnight ride made him an American folk hero. Henry Wadsworth Longfellow told the story in his 1861 poem Paul Revere's Ride.
The Declaration of Independence was first read in public on July 8, 1776. It was read at noon in three places: Trenton, Easton and Philadelphia.
In 1775, the Second Continental Congress made an army, the Continental Army. It chose George Washington to lead it.
In 1787, men met at Independence Hall in Philadelphia. They wrote the Constitution there.
The U.S. Constitution is the oldest written national constitution still in use in the world.
The Bill of Rights is the first ten amendments to the United States Constitution.
The 55 delegates who drafted the Constitution are among the men known as the Founding Fathers of the new nation.
The 9th Amendment says that a right is not missing just because it is not listed in the Bill of Rights.
George Washington was the first U.S. president. Every vote of the Electoral College elected him in 1789 and again in 1792.
Abraham Lincoln was born in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky on February 12, 1809.
On January 1, 1863, Lincoln said that slaves in the rebel states were free. This was the Emancipation Proclamation.
Theodore Roosevelt was 42 years old when he was first inaugurated. That made him the youngest person to hold the office of president.
Theodore Roosevelt won the 1906 Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to end the Russo-Japanese War. He was the first non-European to win a Nobel Prize.
Hiking with his family in the Alps in 1869, Theodore Roosevelt found that exercise helped his asthma and lifted his spirits.
The White House was built between 1792 and 1800. Its outside walls are Aquia Creek sandstone painted white.
Americans argued about slavery for years. In 1860, Abraham Lincoln was elected president. He did not want slavery to spread.
On April 9, 1865, General Lee surrendered to General Grant at Appomattox Court House. That began the end of the war.
Lincoln's Gettysburg Address was only 271 words long and ten sentences. The speaker before him talked for two hours and used 13,607 words.
Harriet Tubman escaped slavery. Then she made some 13 trips to rescue about 70 enslaved people.
Harriet Tubman guided a raid at Combahee Ferry. It freed more than 700 enslaved people.
The Emancipation Proclamation changed the lives of more than 3.5 million enslaved people. It made them free.
The California gold rush began on January 24, 1848, when gold was found by James W. Marshall.
The news of gold brought about 300,000 people to California. They came from the rest of the United States and from other countries.
San Francisco grew from a small settlement of about 200 people in 1846 to a boomtown of about 36,000 people by 1852.
The Oregon Trail was a wagon route 2,170 mi (3,490 km) long. It connected the Missouri River to valleys in Oregon Territory.
Use of the Oregon Trail declined after the first transcontinental railroad was completed in 1869. The railroad made the trip west faster, cheaper and safer.
Pony Express riders could not weigh more than 125 lb (57 kg). The riders changed about every 75 to 100 mi (120 to 160 km), and they rode day and night.
From 1892 to 1954, about 12 million immigrants who arrived at the Port of New York and New Jersey were processed at Ellis Island.
Ellis Island is named after Samuel Ellis. He was a Welshman who bought the island in 1774.
The Statue of Liberty was dedicated on October 28, 1886. In her left hand she carries a tablet marked July 4, 1776, in Roman numerals.
The Mayflower was an English sailing ship, 110 ft (34 m) long and 25 ft (7.5 m) wide. In 1620 she carried a group of English families, known today as the Pilgrims, to the New World.
After 10 weeks at sea, the Mayflower reached what is now the United States. It carried 102 passengers and a crew of about 30. It dropped anchor near the tip of Cape Cod in November 1620.
The first inspection station on Ellis Island opened in 1892. A fire destroyed it in 1897.
In 1872, the United States set up Yellowstone National Park. It was the first public park for the benefit and enjoyment of the people.
The Yellowstone Park bison herd is the oldest and largest public bison herd in the United States.
The Grand Canyon is 277 mi (446 km) long and up to 18 mi (29 km) wide. It is over a mile deep, at 6,093 ft (1,857 m).
The North Rim of the Grand Canyon is cooler than the South Rim, because it is higher. It averages 8,000 ft (2,400 m) above sea level.
Old Faithful erupts on average every 92 minutes. The time between eruptions can be as short as 35 minutes or as long as 120 minutes.
An eruption of Old Faithful can shoot 3,700 to 8,400 gallons of boiling water. The water reaches a height of 106 to 185 ft (32 to 56 m).
